chunks: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated via his chain from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) that he said:

Why do you hasten the appearance of al-Qa'im? By Allah, his clothing is not but rough cloth, and his food is not but coarse food, and he is nothing but the sword, and death is under the shadow of the sword.

key_terms.السَّيْفُ: al-Sayf (The Sword), symbolizing military struggle and authority
key_terms.الْجَشْبُ: al-Jashb (Coarse/Simple), referring to basic, unrefined food
key_terms.الْغَلِيظُ: al-Ghalith (Rough/Coarse), referring to simple, non-luxurious clothing
key_terms.الْقَائِمِ: al-Qa'im (The Riser/Imam), referring to the Twelfth Imam in Shia eschatology
key_terms.تَحْتَ ظِلِّ السَّيْفِ: Tahta Zill al-Sayf (Under the shadow of the sword), indicating death in battle or through conflict

ai.seo_question: What was the lifestyle and mode of struggle of Imam al-Qa'im according to Abu Abdullah al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) corrects the common misconception of a luxurious emergence by emphasizing the Mahdi’s austere asceticism (zuhd), characterized by rough clothing and simple sustenance. This hadith underscores the reality of his military leadership (qital), where the sword is not merely a tool but the defining context of his life and inevitable martyrdom, aligning with the Shia expectation of a transformative struggle rather than a passive wait.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (20) Ali bin al-Husayn narrated from Muhammad bin Ali al-Kufi from al-Hasan bin Mahboob from Ali bin Abu Hamza from Abu Baseer that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) had said:
“Why do you urge on the appearance of al-Qa’im? By Allah, he wears rough cloths and eats coarse food. There will be nothing but the sword and killing under the shadow of the sword.”
